insights: Tech and robotics topics outperform space: Tesla, Unitree, and computing Shorts average ~1,100-1,300 views, whereas space Shorts average ~445 views.
Shorts feed delivers 83-95% of views on successful Shorts; the one Short with low feed traffic ('Nuclear Submarines' at 6% feed) flopped with only 51 views.
Explicit calls-to-action cause severe drop-offs in Shorts: pointing viewers to the channel at 38.6s triggered a massive 23.4% retention drop on the Jet Engines Short.
Hooks between 4.8s and 6.9s consistently lose 3-9% of viewers across nearly every Short, indicating opening sentences need to deliver immediate payoff faster.
Audience engagement via comments is practically non-existent across almost all videos (0 to 1 comments), confirming calls-to-comment or closing questions are too weak.
Long-form content data is too thin to draw firm conclusions (only 3 videos), though specific numbers in titles ('at 2,000°C') dramatically outperformed vague phrasing (507 vs 4 views).
The 'Countdown' and 'News' formats reliably secure both high retention (64-68% view percentage) and high volume (1,000+ views) on Shorts.
